title: Volume 7 · Assets, Quality and CRM
subtitle: Lessons 5–8: capitalise and depreciate a van, inspect what arrives, and convert a lead into a priced quotation
outcomes: Capitalise a purchase as an asset and post depreciation every month
Use quality inspection to reject goods before they reach stock
Move a lead through opportunity to a priced quotation without losing the trail
Decide which of these three modules a distributor should switch on first

slides.title: Capitalise the van instead of expensing it
bullets: An asset purchase is a purchase invoice with an asset item, which creates the asset record
Useful life and depreciation method are accounting policy, so get them signed off
Six figures of van on the balance sheet is very different from six figures of expense
Every asset needs a location and a custodian, or the register is fiction

rows: SM-VAN, is fixed asset, asset category Vehicles
Van 60,000.00 from the dealer, no stock effect

slides.notes: Sixty thousand over five years is twelve thousand a year, or one thousand a month, and that is the number the client's accountant will check first. Capitalising also keeps the profit and loss statement readable, because a van is not a January cost. Get the category approved in writing before the first invoice, since changing depreciation method later means a restatement.

slides.title: Post depreciation monthly, not annually in a panic
bullets: Depreciation is a journal the system generates from the schedule
Straight line on sixty thousand over five years is one thousand a month
Accumulated depreciation is a separate account, so the asset keeps its cost
Year-end catch-up postings are a symptom of a missing monthly routine

rows: Same routine on the last day

slides.notes: After twelve months the net book value is forty eight thousand, and the depreciation expense for the year is twelve thousand. Ask the learner to state both before opening the report, because those two figures are what the auditor tests. If the client only posts at year end, the monthly management accounts are wrong all year, which undermines every other number the consultant produced.

slides.title: Inspect what arrives before it becomes stock
bullets: Quality inspection sits between the receipt and the warehouse when configured that way
Rejected quantity stays out of sellable stock, which is the entire point
Each inspection needs parameters with numeric ranges, or it is a tick box
Quality results feed the supplier conversation, so keep them per supplier

rows: Visual check, parameters Appearance and Function
9 accepted, 1 rejected for a cracked housing

slides.notes: One rejected unit means nine accepted, and the supplier conversation now has a document behind it. Quality is often sold as a compliance feature, but its real value in distribution is the argument it wins with a supplier who disputes a return. If a client rejects inspection as bureaucracy, ask them what evidence they use today.

slides.title: From lead to opportunity to priced quotation
bullets: A lead is an unqualified contact; an opportunity is a deal with a value and a date
Converting keeps the trail, which is what makes pipeline reporting possible
The quotation carries the price, and it is the first document a customer sees
Every opportunity needs a probability and a territory, or the pipeline report lies

rows: Aeon Big, contact and source Trade show

slides.notes: Sixty per cent of twenty four hundred is fourteen hundred forty, and that weighted number is what a sales director actually manages. Without probability and territory, the pipeline report is a list of hopes. The quotation itself is ordinary work, but the trail from lead to opportunity to quotation to order is what lets the owner see conversion rates for the first time.

slides.title: Schedule, ledger and register agree
bullets: The asset, the ledger and the register must show the same accumulated amount
Net book value falls by the monthly charge, and the expense sits in the right period
A missed month is visible immediately in the schedule, not at year end
Disposal later depends on this schedule being correct today
slides.notes: Three views of one number again: the schedule, the asset record and the balance sheet. When they agree, the client can file the month without adjustment. When they disagree, the cause is nearly always a depreciation entry posted in a closed period or an asset created after the run date, and both are one-minute fixes.

slides.title: What the CRM numbers actually prove
bullets: Weighted pipeline equals value times probability, summed across open opportunities
A quotation without an opportunity is a document with no history
Conversion rate is the number a sales director will ask for first
Data quality in CRM is measured by how many fields are blank

rows: leading indicator, not yet a rate

slides.notes: The weighted figure of fourteen hundred forty is the only CRM number a manager should act on weekly, because it changes with probability rather than with optimism. Quotation total of two thousand six hundred forty is where the tax enters and where sales and finance usually disagree. Show both on one page and the pipeline meeting becomes a forecast rather than a wish list.

slides.title: What to switch on first for a distributor
bullets: Assets are mandatory once a client owns vehicles or equipment above their capitalisation threshold
Quality is worth it when returns or supplier disputes are a recurring cost
CRM pays only if someone owns the pipeline weekly, otherwise it becomes a data graveyard
Each module adds a control the client must operate, so sequence them

rows: Any capital purchase above the threshold
Expenses hit one month, audit finding
A named person owns the pipeline

slides.notes: Sequencing is the consultant's judgement call, and this table is the argument to have with the client before the proposal. A distributor with three vans needs assets in phase one; a trader who sells on quotation needs CRM before panels. Say what you would switch on first, and say what you would leave until year two.

slides.title: The three reports that keep these modules honest
bullets: Asset register value must equal the fixed asset control account
Quality rejection rate by supplier is the number that changes behaviour
Pipeline weighted value must match the opportunities it sums, without duplicates
All three are monthly reads, not annual ones

rows: What do we own and what is it worth
What will we sell next month
Is the cost in the right period

slides.notes: Reconciling the asset register to the control account is the same discipline as debtors and creditors, and it takes two minutes a month. Quality rejection rate and weighted pipeline are softer, but each has a single number a manager can act on. Give the client these five rows as the monthly read, and the modules earn their place.

lab.title: Lab · Capitalise a van, depreciate it, inspect a receipt and convert a lead
steps: Create the asset item and purchase the van for 60,000.00 on a purchase invoice
Confirm the asset category produces 1,000.00 of monthly depreciation
Run depreciation for January and confirm net book value of 59,000.00
Confirm the depreciation expense of 1,000.00 in the profit and loss statement
Set up a quality inspection template and attach it to SM-BL200
Receive 10 units, reject 1 and confirm only 9 reach stock
Create a lead for Aeon Big and convert it to a 2,400.00 opportunity
Produce the quotation for 2,640.00 including SST and check the weighted pipeline
lab.done: Done when the van shows 59,000.00 net book value, nine units were received after inspection, and the opportunity carries a 1,440.00 weighted value with a live quotation.

quiz.question: A 60,000.00 asset with a five year straight line life depreciates monthly by what?
quiz.why: 60,000 divided by five years is 12,000 a year, or 1,000.00 a month over twelve periods.

quiz.question: What does the asset register value reconcile to?
quiz.why: The register is the detail behind the control account, so the two must agree, exactly as debtors and creditors do.

quiz.question: After a quality inspection rejects one of ten units, what reaches stock?
quiz.why: Rejected quantity stays out of sellable stock, so only the accepted nine units are received into the warehouse.

quiz.question: A 2,400.00 opportunity at 60 per cent probability has what weighted value?
quiz.why: Weighted value is value times probability, so 2,400 × 0.6 = 1,440.00, which is what the pipeline report should show.

quiz.question: Which module should a distributor with three delivery vans switch on first?
quiz.why: Vehicles above the capitalisation threshold must be capitalised and depreciated, or the profit and loss statement carries a distorted one-off cost.

memory.spine: Capitalise, depreciate, inspect and qualify: four modules, one habit of proving each of them against a register and a report.

device.label: Capitalise, depreciate, inspect, qualify
expansion: Capitalise: a purchase invoice with an asset item creates the Asset record
Depreciate: a journal generated from the schedule, monthly, not once in a December panic
Inspect: Quality Inspection sits between the receipt and the warehouse when configured
Qualify: lead, then opportunity, then a priced quotation
Asset register, ledger and schedule must show the same accumulated amount

cards.q: How is a van capitalised rather than expensed?
cards.a: With a purchase invoice whose item is marked as a fixed asset, which creates the Asset record.

cards.q: Where does accumulated depreciation have to agree?
cards.a: In three places: the asset register, the depreciation account in the ledger and the schedule.
A lead is an unqualified contact, an opportunity is a deal with a value, a date and a probability.
Sum of value times probability across all open opportunities.

cards.q: When does a quality inspection happen?
cards.a: On receipt, before the goods become available stock, when the item is configured that way.

trap.what: Depreciation is posted once a year as a single large journal in December.
trap.why: Eleven months of the profit and loss are wrong and the register never matched the ledger in between, so nobody could catch it early.

narration: Three modules that clients ask for and rarely operate properly. Fixed assets first: sixty thousand of van becomes twelve thousand a year, one thousand a month, and the register must agree with the control account every month. Quality second: an inspection that rejects one of ten units is the difference between an argument with a supplier and a documented claim. CRM third, and only if somebody owns the pipeline: a lead becomes an opportunity with a value and a probability, twenty four hundred at sixty per cent is fourteen hundred forty, and the quotation is the first document the customer sees. Each module adds a control the client has to run, so sequence them and say plainly what you would leave until year two. Assets and quality carry a control that runs itself once configured; CRM only works when a person owns it, so name that person in the workshop before you switch it on, and put the weekly pipeline review in the same meeting as the sales forecast.
